correctness.rationale: Full proof reconstructs natural-basis monomiality from square-basis independence, derives exact scalar equations, proves the q-1 cycle graph equivalence, and gives an explicit GI many-one reduction to simple algebras with a unique hub and invertible block structure. The bundled checker independently compares algebra and graph isomorphism tests for 2,565 two-dimensional pairs over fields 2,3,4 and checks all 75 simple graphs through order 4. Limits of finite verification are stated.

originality.rationale: The October 15, 2026 motivating survey expressly leaves the computational-complexity comparison as Question 50. Monomial rigidity and graph-algebra construction are prior mathematics, but the fixed-q polynomial-size colored-graph encoding together with a simple-algebra GI-hardness construction supply a two-sided GI-completeness theorem not asserted by the primary works compared. The 2019 total-colored graph from all algebra vectors is generally exponential in dimension and is an isotopy functor, not the presented polynomial isomorphism equivalence. Historical novelty is qualified, never presented as independently certified.
residual_risks: A previously published efficient fixed-field isomorphism encoding might exist under a different computational-algebra vocabulary.
The full Elduque–Labra primary texts were not inspected; only their abstracts and 2026 survey descriptions were available.

The graph-to-simple-algebra hardness ingredient may be implicitly recoverable from the 2026 survey construction; originality attaches to the complete two-direction complexity theorem, not to basic graph encoding or monomiality.
The claim does not extend the fixed-field polynomial upper bound to a succinct variable-field input model.

value.rationale: Provides an exact answer to a named 2026 computational-complexity question for every fixed finite field; the simple-algebra restriction retains GI hardness, so nonsimplicity is not responsible. The \(n(q-1)\)-vertex colored reduction gives a dimension-controlled algorithmic translation useful in explicit classification. The general result is an all-dimensional equivalence, not an arbitrary small benchmark or a routine numerical gain.
